subtype: Boss expects excellence or expects nothing [Receiver]

Wei and Tuan started as summer interns at the same Hanoi engineering firm on the same Monday. By the second week, the difference was clear. Ms Lan stopped by Wei's desk every afternoon: "Try the drainage plan for Block B. I'll mark it up tomorrow, and I'll be honest." Her red notes were long and sometimes stung.
Tuan, seated at the far end of the office, was asked to scan old drawings and order lunch. Nobody checked his work, because nobody expected much. By August, Wei was presenting a section at the client meeting. Tuan had learned where every file was and little else.
On the last day he told his mother, "I think I'm just not an engineer." He never found out that Ms Lan had simply decided, on day one, which of them looked keen.

qa.a: They sometimes stung, but the honest feedback pushed Wei to improve until presenting at the client meeting.

Saturday night.
Seema's engagement photos went up today. Palace hotel, sunset, a ring the size of a chickpea. She'd texted me last week, "Neelam, you're coming to the party na?" By the fifth photo I was sitting on my bed thinking, what am I even doing with my life? One-room flat, nobody special, same job.
Then I did the thing I promised myself. I closed the app and asked: what does my life look like next to MY last year, not Seema's best evening? Last year I was jobless and scared. This year I have a job I like, rent paid on my own, and I finished my first half-marathon.
And the photos are one evening. Last month she told me she's anxious about her in-laws. None of that is in the sunset.
Sent her a heart. Meant it.

qa.a: Neelam felt small and discouraged, measuring a whole ordinary life against Seema's best evening.

qa.a: Neelam's own last year; it shows real progress, like a new job and a half-marathon, instead of someone's highlights.
